status_summary: DOT and NHTSA announced an AV Framework on 2025-04-24 and have since acted on parts of the NHTSA recommendation but not on the Standing General Order reversal. NHTSA streamlined crash reporting under the order (third amendment dated 2025-04-24, effective June 2025), extended its exemption program to U.S.-built vehicles, proposed amendments to FMVSS Nos. 102, 103, 104, 110 and 135 for vehicles without manual controls (March to June 2026), and withdrew the AV STEP proposal on 2026-06-26. The Standing General Order remains in force: NHTSA sought a three-year reinstatement of its information collection in 2026 and says it is developing a rule to codify its requirements, which differs from the Mandate's call to reverse it. For trucking, no FMCSA rulemaking was found; FMCSA published an application from Aurora Operations on 2026-04-15 for a five-year exemption from warning-triangle requirements for driverless trucks, which it had not decided in the document read.

timeline.event: DOT and NHTSA announce an automated vehicle framework (DOT press release of this date): crash reporting continues in streamlined form and the exemption program is extended to U.S.-built vehicles. NHTSA's 2026-07-31 notice (last entry) describes three goals for the framework (safe ongoing operations, removing unnecessary regulatory barriers and enabling commercial deployment) and a third amended Standing General Order issued the same day, which streamlines crash reporting for ADS and Level 2 ADAS (effective June 2025): severe crashes reported within five days, less severe ones monthly, duplicate reports and monthly zero reports removed.

NHTSA proposes to amend FMVSS No. 102 (and, in a companion proposal, Nos. 103 and 104) so ADS-equipped vehicles with no manual driving controls are not required to display transmission shift positions, saying this reduces compliance burden without affecting safety; comments closed 2026-04-15. NHTSA describes this as one of several rulemakings for ADS-equipped vehicles.

FMCSA publishes Aurora Operations' application for a five-year exemption allowing Level 4 ADS trucks to use cab-mounted flashing amber beacons instead of warning triangles or fusees; Aurora currently operates under a limited waiver that expires 2026-07-09. FMCSA had not decided the application, and 402 comments were received.

NHTSA submits to OMB a three-year reinstatement of the information collection behind Standing General Order 2021-01 (crash reporting for ADS and Level 2 ADAS), estimating 19,208 burden hours a year versus 31,319 under the prior approval; the order itself continues.

NHTSA withdraws the AV STEP proposed rule (a voluntary safety-reporting program proposed 2025-01-15), citing low expected participation and criticism from both industry and safety groups, and noting that exemption streamlining and SGO changes under the AV Framework serve similar goals. The same day it proposes updating FMVSS No. 135 for ADS-equipped vehicles.

NHTSA publishes AV Framework updates and interim guidance on commercial deployment exemptions under 49 CFR part 555. It reports that the AV Exemption Program now covers U.S.-built vehicles, that a rule to codify the Standing General Order is in development, that proposed rules would update FMVSS Nos. 102, 103, 104, 110 and 135, and that a rulemaking on ADS performance requirements was announced in March 2026; the comment period was later extended (notice of 2026-08-31).

title: Update vehicle and trucking rules for automated vehicles; end mandatory crash reporting
uncertainties: All sources are Federal Register documents read through summaries; no news coverage or web search was used for this record. The FMVSS Nos. 103, 104, 110 and 135 proposals and the 2026-08-31 comment extension were seen in a Federal Register listing and NHTSA's own summary but not read individually. The effective June 2025 date for the third amended order comes from the AV Framework notice; the May 2026 notice did not state it. The seven investigations and seven recalls NHTSA attributes to the order (June 2025 to July 2026) were not used. FMCSA's decision on the Aurora application, the status of the waiver after 2026-07-09, and any FMCSA rulemaking on automated trucks were not found (a short Federal Register query for FMCSA documents mentioning 'automated' returned only the application). The match with the Mandate is partial because the Mandate asked for the Standing General Order to be reversed, not streamlined.
